title: Tensegrity: a three-strut prism designed for a load, and the six-strut classic, from one matrix
question: Where does a tensegrity's shape come from, why does prestress make it stiff, and is there a prestress at which a one-metre three-strut prism carries an 800 N load with no slack cable, no buckled strut and an acceptable sag?
label: A worked study. Not a certified design and not for manufacture. Material values are from memory; see each source.

requirements.shall: The shape shall admit exactly one state of self-stress, with every cable in tension and every strut in compression.
requirements.check: SVD of the equilibrium matrix: s = 1, signs by member kind

requirements.shall: At the design prestress the structure shall be stable: with rigid-body motion removed, the smallest stiffness shall be positive, and it shall be zero when the prestress is zero.
requirements.check: eigenvalues of the tangent stiffness on the supported structure

requirements.shall: Under every load case no cable shall fall below one tenth of its own prestress.
requirements.check: minimum cable tension over 14 load cases, cables allowed to go slack in the solve

requirements.shall: Under every load case no strut shall exceed its Euler buckling load divided by FS_buckling, nor its yield load.
Under every load case no cable shall exceed its minimum breaking load divided by FS_cable.
Under the 800 N press the top shall drop no more than H / 100 and turn no more than 5 degrees; under the 200 N side push no joint shall move more than 5 mm.
The X3D scene shall be the design: every joint and member in the scene shall sit where the bank puts it and carry the bank's forces, by name.

exploration.when: 27 Nov 2026 (US Eastern), before the limits below were written
findings: The smallest stiffness of the supported prism was 163.06, 326.06, 651.90, 1302.9 and 1953.0 N/m at 100, 200, 400, 800 and 1200 N of prestress, and 0 at 0: proportional to prestress. The next stiffness is about 54,000 N/m.
Pressing, lifting and twisting in either sense all raised the tension in every cable and the compression in every strut. Only a load on one joint loosened a cable.
The 800 N press turned the top 4.7 to 6.5 degrees while dropping it 6 to 9 mm: the response is a screw, mostly rotation.
Load against deflection is not a straight line: at 400 N of prestress, 100 N dropped the top 1.82 mm and 800 N dropped it 7.26 mm.
Residuals below about 1e-9 N are rounding (strut EA is 1e7 N), so the solvers stop at 1e-7 N.
